- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., 1.00 or 0.25) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00 with prior lows), model often under-forecasts; adjust downward bias or add lagged support.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or add mean-reversion term.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00, 0.25, 0.33), model often drifts toward trend continuation; apply mean-reversion heuristic or reduce momentum multiplier.
- If true outcome shows strong mean-reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to ignore it — adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average or 20-day SMA.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in upward trend — if sentiment is weak or mixed, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- If sentiment shows reversal (e.g., from +0.25 to -1.00), model often fails to adjust — trigger correction rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% and add downward bias.
